- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts are flat or slightly rising, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >10% from prior period), model tends to overshoot — cap forecast growth to 2–3% per period to avoid overcorrection.  
- If official supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates, model underestimates downside risk — add 1–2% downward bias to forecast mean.  
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model overfits to recent trend — smooth forecast with 3-period moving average to reduce noise.  
- In high-event periods (≥20 events/30d), model often fails to capture event-driven volatility — increase forecast volatility by ±1.5% of mean for next 3 periods.  
- If true outcome deviates >5% from 30d forecast mean, check sentiment history for recent reversal — if sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish, adjust forecast downward by 2–3% immediately.
